title: [Bug]: Renderer Crash (SIGSEGV / SEGV_PKUERR) in 26.0.0, 26.1.0 and 26.2.0
body:

- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

26.2.0

### What operating system are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

25.8.0

### Expected Behavior

The renderer should not crash.

### Actual Behavior

An application I'm working on (which isn't open source yet) crashes on start when using Electron 26.0.0, 26.1.0 or 26.2.0.

The crash dump is always identical. The crashing thread crashed in the function `electron!partition_alloc::internal::PartitionBucket::MaintainActiveList()`.

comments.body:
Thanks for confirming, I wanted to confirm if the BRP feature that was enabled by default on Linux https://<redacted-host>/c/chromium/src/+/4478673 between 114 and 116 was related to the regression. But now that I look at the brp enabled process, it is only set to [kBrowserProcess](https://<redacted-host>/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/116.0.5791.1:base/allocator/partition_alloc_features.cc;l=135) on Linux and given the crash is in renderer per the issue title the feature would be unrelated.


> Regarding the other flag --enable-features=PartitionAllocBackupRefPtr:brp-mode/enabled I wasn't sure how to use it.

You can ignore this flag, it only affects the memory reclaimer code path associated with the BRP feature. The crash you are seeing is from https://<redacted-host>/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/116.0.5845.188:base/allocator/partition_alloc_support.cc;l=1429-1430

I would recommend the following as next steps:

* Backport https://<redacted-host>/c/chromium/src/+/4665034 which isolates the memory reclaimer into a separate feature and you should be able to disable the feature as a temporary workaround to unblock updating to Electron 26
* Since you have E2E repro with signal application, I would suggest to investigate the crash attaching a debugger to the renderer process. The partition allocator entry point for render process is at https://<redacted-host>/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/wtf/allocator/partitions.cc, currently there are 3 different partition roots associated with the renderer, we don't know which root is triggering the crash in `partition_alloc::PartitionRoot::PurgeMemory`. So first step would be to identify the root among https://<redacted-host>/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/wtf/allocator/partitions.h;l=116-118 which can give clue to the application code that triggers the crash.

I did a small foray into it and found out that Debug build just crashes outside of partition allocator :<nick>: I can reproduce the crash consistently on Fedora Linux, but if I delete everything from our preload - it doesn't seem to happen.

I suspect that it could be our Neon rust addons that cause the trouble. Will look more into it today!

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Adding a datapoint: our users are only running into this crash on shared Linux environments (i.e. multiple users, no root access). I also tested on a Debian 11 VM (VMWare Fusion on iMac host, macOS Ventura), and did not experience the crash. In the past, we've had to implement workarounds (`--no-sandbox`) on these kind of shared Debian machines due to `setuid` restrictions.

 Although crash cases reported here and in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/39515 are when `sandbox: false` for the renderer and not the main process. I saw the bisect ranges attached in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/39515#issuecomment-1688830738 but the only thing that stood out was `BackupRefPtr` feature enabled on Linux and again this is not enabled for renderer process so should be unrelated.

@participant1 can you attach the crash stack for https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/39775#issuecomment-1726235269 ? I will add some crash keys to the relevant call sites in a custom electron build as next step.

**PS:** If anyone can provide a reliable repro case using a clean VM even without electron fiddle but rather using a production application, I am happy to set it up.

@participant2 thanks for the build! I first tested whether I can still reproduce the issue with 26.2.2. I put "26.2.2" in `package.json`, started [the app](https://threema.ch/en/download-md) and immediately got a renderer crash.

Then I unpacked your build:

```
$ cd node_modules/electron/dist
$ rm -r *
$ unzip /tmp/electron-v26.2.2-linux-x64-dcheck.zip
```

...and rebuilt our app with it. Now the app takes extremely long to start (I assume due to all the debug logic that was enabled in this build), and... doesn't crash anymore 🙃

As a sanity check, I ran `rm -rf node_modules/ && npm install`, started the app again, and it crashes again.

The parameters I used for starting: `--enable-logging=stderr`.

---

When the application starts, usually a lot of "ui <-> worker" and "worker <-> database" communication takes place. Maybe the debug logic slowed down the app, which resulted in a different memory allocation behavior, and no crash. Or maybe it's a race condition, that wasn't triggered because the code was slower.

Is the log still helpful if the crash wasn't reproduced? I assume not?
